items.title: Forget the generation gap, this budget is about 'the 1 per cent' and the rest
items.description: Just like it did in 2019, Labor is making an argument about wealth in Australia when it proposes negative gearing and capital gains tax changes.

items.title: Labor upgrades migration numbers by 55,000 in federal budget
items.description: The federal budget reveals the government expects more migrants to arrive to Australia than previously thought, even as it faces a campaign from the Coalition and One Nation to slash migration rates.

items.title: Is the 2026 budget a missed opportunity for First Nations people?
items.description: First Nations experts have their say on whether the $1.2 billion for Closing the Gap initiatives announced in this year's budget is likely to hit the mark.

items.title: Donald Trump arrives in Beijing ahead of Xi Jinping summit
items.description: The ​US and China are expected to agree to forums to facilitate mutual trade and investment.

items.title: Shots fired in Philippine senate as ICC seeks to arrest ex-police chief
items.description: Multiple gun shots have been heard at the senate building in the Philippines with people told to run for cover.

items.title: UK MP Nigel Farage facing inquiry over $9m gift from crypto billionaire
items.description: Britain's parliamentary watchdog will begin an investigation into whether Reform UK leader Nigel Farage, breached its rules by accepting a 5 million pound ($9.31 million) gift which he did not declare.

items.title: What's in the federal budget for older Australians?
items.description: Despite it being an intergenerational budget, specific parts of the economic strategy will impact older Australians.

items.title: NSW premier attacks 'kangaroo court' after report into $37m grants scheme
items.description: Chris Minns responds to claims from a parliamentary inquiry that the government "unlawfully redirected" millions of dollars of public money and accused witnesses of lying under oath.

items.title: 'Handing miners key to bulldozer': Expert slams native title compensation
items.description: Andrew Forrest's Fortescue has been ordered to hand over the largest native title compensation payout in Australian history. But some say it falls painfully short of what is owed.

items.title: Kate tours Italy in first overseas visit since cancer recovery
items.description: The royal is visiting Reggio Emilia, the Italian city famed for its approach to early childhood education.

items.title: At least 12 people killed in Israeli strikes on cars in Lebanon
items.description: The deadly drone strikes come on the eve of a new round of peace talks between Israel and Lebanon in the United States.

items.title: New report accuses Hamas of 'deliberately' using rape on October 7
items.description: A 300-page report from an Israeli non-profit organisation has detailed allegations of horrific sexual assault against victims of Hamas's October 7, 2023, attacks on Israel, accusing the group of "systematically and deliberately" using rape and sexual torture.

items.title: Six dead as Russia launches over 800 drones at Ukraine
items.description: Volodymyr Zelenskyy accuses Russia of attempting to overload Ukraine's defences in an hours-long onslaught.

items.title: Commonwealth Bank shares slump 10.4pc in biggest one-day fall on record
items.description: It was the worst day on the stock market for Australia's biggest bank since March 2020, when it dropped about 10 per cent, with sentiment also weighed by a trading update and broader weakness in bank stocks.

items.title: How Broadbeach became a blues mecca
items.description: As some festivals crumble, the Gold Coast's mayor says the 25-year-old Blues On Broadbeach event isn't going anywhere.

items.title: NT government accused of 'politicising tragedy' with child protection laws
items.description: Peak Aboriginal bodies have accused the Northern Territory government of using Kumanjayi Little Baby's alleged murder as political cover to push ahead with sweeping changes to child protection laws.

items.title: Australian government secures aircraft to fly home Hantavirus cruise passengers
items.description: A suitable aircraft to bring home passengers from the Hantavirus-hit cruise has been secured and will repatriate the group of six later this week.

items.title: Inquiry witness claims CFMEU planted asbestos to get project shut down
items.description: The inquiry heard the CFMEU was making social media posts attacking the credibility of WHSQ employees.

items.title: Graphic novel wins $60k Stella Prize for first time in award's 14-year history
items.description: Lee Lai's debut graphic novel, Stone Fruit, was longlisted for the Stella Prize in 2022. Four years on, she's won the prestigious award for her latest book, Cannon.

items.title: Eurovision pays musical homage to Austria-Australia confusion
items.description: The first semifinal of the Eurovision Song Contest includes a comedic musical interlude about the differences between Austria and Australia and sends 10 countries through to the grand final on Saturday.

items.title: The pianist fighting the MSO over right to bring whole self to stage
items.description: In 2024, Jayson Gillham's show was cancelled for his on-stage comments about Palestine. Now he brings a legal suit and a new recital tour with a Palestinian Jordanian artist.

items.title: Invictus Australia budget cut labelled potentially 'life-threatening'
items.description: The federal government is urged to reverse its decision to cut funding to Invictus Australia, an organisation that supports veterans.

items.title: NT Police fraud squad seizes grenades, warheads in raids south of Darwin
items.description: Northern Territory Police have seized 32 explosive ordnance items, including hand grenades, rocket components and warheads in raids south of Darwin.

items.title: 'We don’t want these people': Minorities fearful after One Nation victory
items.description: David Farley has won Farrer for One Nation in a landslide, but there are some in the community yet to be convinced of his ability to represent them.

items.title: Protesters demand 'stop the chop' at rally opposing North Adelaide golf project
items.description: More than 2,000 people gathered at Parliament House in Adelaide to protest against the chopping down of trees to make way for the North Adelaide Golf Course redevelopment.
